review_state: former source tie retracted; revised source endpoints unmeasured
drawing_observation: A renewed native sheet-2 read shows D35.4 reaching D42.10/D37.13 at a filled junction. D37.12 is on separate upper conductor 3, the same numbered rail as D42.9/D43.9 CK; D37.11 descends independently near x2400. The prior D35.4/D37.11 tie was a tracing error.
component_observation: The registered bottom-notch D37 field fixes pin 11 as the fourth contact down on its left image column. The marked top-notch D35 field fixes pin 4 as the fourth contact down on its left column. Both have visible local front-copper departures, but no uninterrupted front trace between these contacts can be followed through the white-wire corridor and package region. Nearby via and trace features are not enough to assign a remote connection.
solder_observation: The overlapping tile shows multiple parallel solder traces and two package fields around the projected D35/D37 area. D35.13 has a separate search registration in d35-pin13-photo-review.json, but no independent D37.11-to-D35.4 two-face pad registration or continuous solder path is established here.
decision: Retain the corrected D35.4/D42.10/D37.13 drawing junction and D37.12 numbered-3 clock rail in the source model. Keep owner-board continuity and D37.11 remote endpoint pending.
next_inspection: With power removed, meter D35.4 directly to D42.10 and D37.13 in both polarities; test D37.12 against D42.9/D43.9, and D37.11 for isolation from both groups and R38.1/SHIFT_G. Treat a semiconductor-path reading as inconclusive until the copper path is isolated.
